solution.lib/chapter_marks.rb:
module ChapterMarks
  TS = /\A(?:([0-9]{1,3}):([0-5][0-9])|([0-9]{1,3})):([0-5][0-9])(?:\.([0-9]{1,3}))?\z/
  BLANKS = " \t"

  def self.parse_ts(text)
    m = TS.match(text)
    raise ArgumentError, 'bad timestamp' if m.nil?
    total = if m[1]
              (m[1].to_i * 60 + m[2].to_i) * 60 + m[4].to_i
            else
              m[3].to_i * 60 + m[4].to_i
            end
    total * 1000 + (m[5] ? m[5].ljust(3, '0').to_i : 0)
  end

  def self.fmt_ts(ms)
    raise ArgumentError, 'negative time' if ms < 0
    secs, milli = ms.divmod(1000)
    mins, sec = secs.divmod(60)
    hours, minute = mins.divmod(60)
    format('%02d:%02d:%02d.%03d', hours, minute, sec, milli)
  end

  def self.trim(text)
    a = 0
    b = text.length
    a += 1 while a < b && BLANKS.include?(text[a])
    b -= 1 while b > a && BLANKS.include?(text[b - 1])
    text[a...b]
  end

  def self.collapse(title)
    out = +''
    pending = false
    title.each_char do |ch|
      if BLANKS.include?(ch)
        pending = !out.empty?
      else
        if pending
          out << ' '
          pending = false
        end
        out << ch
      end
    end
    out
  end

  def self.chapters(text)
    items = []
    text.gsub("\r\n", "\n").split("\n", -1).each do |raw|
      line = trim(raw)
      next if line.empty? || line[0] == '#'
      cut = 0
      cut += 1 while cut < line.length && !BLANKS.include?(line[cut])
      title = collapse(trim(line[cut..]))
      raise ArgumentError, 'bad chapter title' if title.empty? || title.length > 200
      items << [parse_ts(line[0...cut]), title]
    end
    items = items.each_with_index.sort_by { |(ms, _), i| [ms, i] }.map(&:first)
    raise ArgumentError, 'the first chapter must start at 0' if items.empty? || items[0][0] != 0
    items.each_cons(2) { |a, b| raise ArgumentError, 'same start' if a[0] == b[0] }
    items
  end

  def self.normalize(text)
    chapters(text).map { |ms, title| "#{fmt_ts(ms)} #{title}" }.join("\n")
  end

  def self.durations(text, total_ms)
    items = chapters(text)
    raise ArgumentError, 'total is not after the last chapter start' if total_ms <= items[-1][0]
    starts = items.map(&:first) + [total_ms]
    starts.each_cons(2).map { |a, b| b - a }
  end

  def self.chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)
    items = chapters(text)
    raise ArgumentError, 'time out of range' if ms < 0 || ms >= total_ms || total_ms <= items[-1][0]
    title = items[0][1]
    items.each { |start, name| title = name if start <= ms }
    title
  end
end

start.README.md:
# podcast chapter marks

A podcast tool reads chapter lists typed by hand, normalises them and answers duration and lookup questions; the timestamp and white-space rules must come out identically in every language.

This repository holds the Python implementation (`chapter_marks.py`). It is being ported to Ruby; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Podcast chapters are written one per line as `<timestamp> <title>`. Everything is counted in **milliseconds**.

* **Timestamps** have two forms: `H:MM:SS` with 1 to 3 hour digits and exactly two digits each for minutes and seconds (minutes and seconds 00..59), or `M:SS` with 1 to 3 minute digits (any value, so `75:30` is allowed) and two second digits (00..59).
  Either may end in a fraction: a `.` and 1 to 3 digits, padded on the right with zeros (`.5` is 500 ms, `.05` is 50 ms, `.123` is 123 ms). ASCII digits only; no signs, no spaces. `parse_ts(text)` returns the milliseconds, anything else is an error.
* `fmt_ts(ms)` is the canonical text `HH:MM:SS.mmm` (hours at least two digits, no upper limit: `3600000` is `01:00:00.000`, `360000000` is `100:00:00.000`); a negative `ms` is an error.
* **Chapter lists.** *White space* is a space or a tab and nothing else (a no-break space or a carriage return in the middle of a title is just a character). Lines end with `\n` or `\r\n`; a line is skipped when it is empty after trimming white space or when its first non-blank character is `#`.
  Every other line is a timestamp, then at least one white space character, then the title: it is trimmed, and every run of white space inside it becomes one space. A title must have 1 to 200 characters (Unicode code points) after that. A line without a title or with a bad timestamp is an error.
* `normalize(text)` sorts the chapters by time (equal times keep their order) and writes them as `fmt_ts(ms) + " " + title` joined by `\n` (no final newline). It is an error when there are no chapters, when two chapters have the same time, or when the earliest does not start at 0.
* `durations(text, total_ms)` is the length of every chapter in sorted order: the next start minus its own start, the last one up to `total_ms`; `total_ms` must be greater than the last start (else an error).
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` is the title of the chapter that contains the time `ms` (a chapter lasts from its start up to, not including, the next start), with `0 <= ms < total_ms` (else an error); the same list rules apply.

## Functions

* `parse_ts(text)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `fmt_ts(ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`ms`: int)
* `normalize(text)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `durations(text, total_ms)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `total_ms`: int)
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `ms`: int, `total_ms`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Python (source)

```python
def parse_ts(text: str) -> int
def fmt_ts(ms: int) -> str
def normalize(text: str) -> str
def durations(text: str, total_ms: int) -> list[int]
def chapter_at(text: str, ms: int, total_ms: int) -> str
```

## Ruby (target)

Create `lib/chapter_marks.rb` (and any extra files you need).

Module `ChapterMarks` in `lib/chapter_marks.rb` with module-level methods (`def self.name`). Failure is signalled by raising a `StandardError`. An absent `opt` value is `nil`.

```ruby
ChapterMarks.parse_ts(text)   # -> Integer
ChapterMarks.fmt_ts(ms)   # -> String
ChapterMarks.normalize(text)   # -> String
ChapterMarks.durations(text, total_ms)   # -> Array<Integer>
ChapterMarks.chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)   # -> String
```

## Checking

`test/test_vectors.rb` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Ruby API; run `the Ruby test script (`test/test_vectors.rb`)`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.
start.test/test_vectors.rb:
require 'json'
require 'chapter_marks'

file = File.exist?('vectors/full.json') ? 'vectors/full.json' : 'vectors/examples.json'
cases = JSON.parse(File.read(file, encoding: 'utf-8'))['cases']
mod = Object.const_get('ChapterMarks')
bad = []
cases.each do |c|
  label = "#{c['fn']}(#{c['args'].map { |a| JSON.generate(a) }.join(', ')})"
  unless mod.respond_to?(c['fn'])
    bad << "missing function #{c['fn']}"
    next
  end
  got = nil
  failed = false
  begin
    got = mod.public_send(c['fn'], *c['args'])
  rescue StandardError, NotImplementedError
    failed = true
  end
  if c['error']
    bad << "#{label}: expected an error, got #{JSON.generate(got)}" unless failed
  elsif failed
    bad << "#{label}: unexpected error, want #{JSON.generate(c['want'])}"
  elsif JSON.generate(got) != JSON.generate(c['want'])
    bad << "#{label}: want #{JSON.generate(c['want'])}, got #{JSON.generate(got)}"
  end
end
unless bad.empty?
  puts "#{bad.size} of #{cases.size} vectors failed:"
  bad.first(8).each { |b| puts "  #{b}" }
  exit 1
end
puts "ok #{cases.size} vectors"

start.README.md:
# podcast chapter marks

A podcast tool reads chapter lists typed by hand, normalises them and answers duration and lookup questions; the timestamp and white-space rules must come out identically in every language.

This repository holds the Ruby implementation (`lib/chapter_marks.rb`). It is being ported to TypeScript; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Podcast chapters are written one per line as `<timestamp> <title>`. Everything is counted in **milliseconds**.

* **Timestamps** have two forms: `H:MM:SS` with 1 to 3 hour digits and exactly two digits each for minutes and seconds (minutes and seconds 00..59), or `M:SS` with 1 to 3 minute digits (any value, so `75:30` is allowed) and two second digits (00..59).
  Either may end in a fraction: a `.` and 1 to 3 digits, padded on the right with zeros (`.5` is 500 ms, `.05` is 50 ms, `.123` is 123 ms). ASCII digits only; no signs, no spaces. `parse_ts(text)` returns the milliseconds, anything else is an error.
* `fmt_ts(ms)` is the canonical text `HH:MM:SS.mmm` (hours at least two digits, no upper limit: `3600000` is `01:00:00.000`, `360000000` is `100:00:00.000`); a negative `ms` is an error.
* **Chapter lists.** *White space* is a space or a tab and nothing else (a no-break space or a carriage return in the middle of a title is just a character). Lines end with `\n` or `\r\n`; a line is skipped when it is empty after trimming white space or when its first non-blank character is `#`.
  Every other line is a timestamp, then at least one white space character, then the title: it is trimmed, and every run of white space inside it becomes one space. A title must have 1 to 200 characters (Unicode code points) after that. A line without a title or with a bad timestamp is an error.
* `normalize(text)` sorts the chapters by time (equal times keep their order) and writes them as `fmt_ts(ms) + " " + title` joined by `\n` (no final newline). It is an error when there are no chapters, when two chapters have the same time, or when the earliest does not start at 0.
* `durations(text, total_ms)` is the length of every chapter in sorted order: the next start minus its own start, the last one up to `total_ms`; `total_ms` must be greater than the last start (else an error).
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` is the title of the chapter that contains the time `ms` (a chapter lasts from its start up to, not including, the next start), with `0 <= ms < total_ms` (else an error); the same list rules apply.

## Functions

* `parse_ts(text)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `fmt_ts(ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`ms`: int)
* `normalize(text)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `durations(text, total_ms)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `total_ms`: int)
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `ms`: int, `total_ms`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Ruby (source)

```ruby
ChapterMarks.parse_ts(text)   # -> Integer
ChapterMarks.fmt_ts(ms)   # -> String
ChapterMarks.normalize(text)   # -> String
ChapterMarks.durations(text, total_ms)   # -> Array<Integer>
ChapterMarks.chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)   # -> String
```

## TypeScript (target)

Create `src/chapter_marks.ts` (and any extra files you need).

Module `src/chapter_marks.ts` with one `export function` per function. The test run includes `tsc -p .` with `strict` enabled, so the code must type-check. Numbers are `number`; `u32` values are non-negative integers below 2^32. Failure is signalled by throwing an exception. An absent `opt` value is `null`.

```ts
export function parseTs(text: string): number
export function fmtTs(ms: number): string
export function normalize(text: string): string
export function durations(text: string, totalMs: number): number[]
export function chapterAt(text: string, ms: number, totalMs: number): string
```

## Checking

`test/vectors.test.ts` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the TypeScript API; run `tsc -p . && node --test build/test/*.test.js`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

module ChapterMarks
  TS = /\A(?:([0-9]{1,3}):([0-5][0-9])|([0-9]{1,3})):([0-5][0-9])(?:\.([0-9]{1,3}))?\z/
  BLANKS = " \t"

  def self.parse_ts(text)
    m = TS.match(text)
    raise ArgumentError, 'bad timestamp' if m.nil?
    total = if m[1]
              (m[1].to_i * 60 + m[2].to_i) * 60 + m[4].to_i
            else
              m[3].to_i * 60 + m[4].to_i
            end
    total * 1000 + (m[5] ? m[5].ljust(3, '0').to_i : 0)
  end

  def self.fmt_ts(ms)
    raise ArgumentError, 'negative time' if ms < 0
    secs, milli = ms.divmod(1000)
    mins, sec = secs.divmod(60)
    hours, minute = mins.divmod(60)
    format('%02d:%02d:%02d.%03d', hours, minute, sec, milli)
  end

  def self.trim(text)
    a = 0
    b = text.length
    a += 1 while a < b && BLANKS.include?(text[a])
    b -= 1 while b > a && BLANKS.include?(text[b - 1])
    text[a...b]
  end

  def self.collapse(title)
    out = +''
    pending = false
    title.each_char do |ch|
      if BLANKS.include?(ch)
        pending = !out.empty?
      else
        if pending
          out << ' '
          pending = false
        end
        out << ch
      end
    end
    out
  end

  def self.chapters(text)
    items = []
    text.gsub("\r\n", "\n").split("\n", -1).each do |raw|
      line = trim(raw)
      next if line.empty? || line[0] == '#'
      cut = 0
      cut += 1 while cut < line.length && !BLANKS.include?(line[cut])
      title = collapse(trim(line[cut..]))
      raise ArgumentError, 'bad chapter title' if title.empty? || title.length > 200
      items << [parse_ts(line[0...cut]), title]
    end
    items = items.each_with_index.sort_by { |(ms, _), i| [ms, i] }.map(&:first)
    raise ArgumentError, 'the first chapter must start at 0' if items.empty? || items[0][0] != 0
    items.each_cons(2) { |a, b| raise ArgumentError, 'same start' if a[0] == b[0] }
    items
  end

  def self.normalize(text)
    chapters(text).map { |ms, title| "#{fmt_ts(ms)} #{title}" }.join("\n")
  end

  def self.durations(text, total_ms)
    items = chapters(text)
    raise ArgumentError, 'total is not after the last chapter start' if total_ms <= items[-1][0]
    starts = items.map(&:first) + [total_ms]
    starts.each_cons(2).map { |a, b| b - a }
  end

  def self.chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)
    items = chapters(text)
    raise ArgumentError, 'time out of range' if ms < 0 || ms >= total_ms || total_ms <= items[-1][0]
    title = items[0][1]
    items.each { |start, name| title = name if start <= ms }
    title
  end
end

require 'json'
require 'chapter_marks'

file = File.exist?('vectors/full.json') ? 'vectors/full.json' : 'vectors/examples.json'
cases = JSON.parse(File.read(file, encoding: 'utf-8'))['cases']
mod = Object.const_get('ChapterMarks')
bad = []
cases.each do |c|
  label = "#{c['fn']}(#{c['args'].map { |a| JSON.generate(a) }.join(', ')})"
  unless mod.respond_to?(c['fn'])
    bad << "missing function #{c['fn']}"
    next
  end
  got = nil
  failed = false
  begin
    got = mod.public_send(c['fn'], *c['args'])
  rescue StandardError, NotImplementedError
    failed = true
  end
  if c['error']
    bad << "#{label}: expected an error, got #{JSON.generate(got)}" unless failed
  elsif failed
    bad << "#{label}: unexpected error, want #{JSON.generate(c['want'])}"
  elsif JSON.generate(got) != JSON.generate(c['want'])
    bad << "#{label}: want #{JSON.generate(c['want'])}, got #{JSON.generate(got)}"
  end
end
unless bad.empty?
  puts "#{bad.size} of #{cases.size} vectors failed:"
  bad.first(8).each { |b| puts "  #{b}" }
  exit 1
end
puts "ok #{cases.size} vectors"

start.README.md:
# podcast chapter marks

A podcast tool reads chapter lists typed by hand, normalises them and answers duration and lookup questions; the timestamp and white-space rules must come out identically in every language.

This repository holds the TypeScript implementation (`src/chapter_marks.ts`). It is being ported to Python; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Podcast chapters are written one per line as `<timestamp> <title>`. Everything is counted in **milliseconds**.

* **Timestamps** have two forms: `H:MM:SS` with 1 to 3 hour digits and exactly two digits each for minutes and seconds (minutes and seconds 00..59), or `M:SS` with 1 to 3 minute digits (any value, so `75:30` is allowed) and two second digits (00..59).
  Either may end in a fraction: a `.` and 1 to 3 digits, padded on the right with zeros (`.5` is 500 ms, `.05` is 50 ms, `.123` is 123 ms). ASCII digits only; no signs, no spaces. `parse_ts(text)` returns the milliseconds, anything else is an error.
* `fmt_ts(ms)` is the canonical text `HH:MM:SS.mmm` (hours at least two digits, no upper limit: `3600000` is `01:00:00.000`, `360000000` is `100:00:00.000`); a negative `ms` is an error.
* **Chapter lists.** *White space* is a space or a tab and nothing else (a no-break space or a carriage return in the middle of a title is just a character). Lines end with `\n` or `\r\n`; a line is skipped when it is empty after trimming white space or when its first non-blank character is `#`.
  Every other line is a timestamp, then at least one white space character, then the title: it is trimmed, and every run of white space inside it becomes one space. A title must have 1 to 200 characters (Unicode code points) after that. A line without a title or with a bad timestamp is an error.
* `normalize(text)` sorts the chapters by time (equal times keep their order) and writes them as `fmt_ts(ms) + " " + title` joined by `\n` (no final newline). It is an error when there are no chapters, when two chapters have the same time, or when the earliest does not start at 0.
* `durations(text, total_ms)` is the length of every chapter in sorted order: the next start minus its own start, the last one up to `total_ms`; `total_ms` must be greater than the last start (else an error).
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` is the title of the chapter that contains the time `ms` (a chapter lasts from its start up to, not including, the next start), with `0 <= ms < total_ms` (else an error); the same list rules apply.

## Functions

* `parse_ts(text)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `fmt_ts(ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`ms`: int)
* `normalize(text)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `durations(text, total_ms)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `total_ms`: int)
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `ms`: int, `total_ms`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## TypeScript (source)

```ts
export function parseTs(text: string): number
export function fmtTs(ms: number): string
export function normalize(text: string): string
export function durations(text: string, totalMs: number): number[]
export function chapterAt(text: string, ms: number, totalMs: number): string
```

## Python (target)

The Python API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Module `chapter_marks` (file `chapter_marks.py` at the repository root). Plain `int`/`str`/`list` values. Failure is signalled by raising an exception (any subclass of `Exception`).

```python
def parse_ts(text: str) -> int
def fmt_ts(ms: int) -> str
def normalize(text: str) -> str
def durations(text: str, total_ms: int) -> list[int]
def chapter_at(text: str, ms: int, total_ms: int) -> str
```

## Checking

`tests/test_vectors.py` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Python API; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# podcast chapter marks

A podcast tool reads chapter lists typed by hand, normalises them and answers duration and lookup questions; the timestamp and white-space rules must come out identically in every language.

This repository holds the Python implementation (`chapter_marks.py`). It is being ported to TypeScript; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Podcast chapters are written one per line as `<timestamp> <title>`. Everything is counted in **milliseconds**.

* **Timestamps** have two forms: `H:MM:SS` with 1 to 3 hour digits and exactly two digits each for minutes and seconds (minutes and seconds 00..59), or `M:SS` with 1 to 3 minute digits (any value, so `75:30` is allowed) and two second digits (00..59).
  Either may end in a fraction: a `.` and 1 to 3 digits, padded on the right with zeros (`.5` is 500 ms, `.05` is 50 ms, `.123` is 123 ms). ASCII digits only; no signs, no spaces. `parse_ts(text)` returns the milliseconds, anything else is an error.
* `fmt_ts(ms)` is the canonical text `HH:MM:SS.mmm` (hours at least two digits, no upper limit: `3600000` is `01:00:00.000`, `360000000` is `100:00:00.000`); a negative `ms` is an error.
* **Chapter lists.** *White space* is a space or a tab and nothing else (a no-break space or a carriage return in the middle of a title is just a character). Lines end with `\n` or `\r\n`; a line is skipped when it is empty after trimming white space or when its first non-blank character is `#`.
  Every other line is a timestamp, then at least one white space character, then the title: it is trimmed, and every run of white space inside it becomes one space. A title must have 1 to 200 characters (Unicode code points) after that. A line without a title or with a bad timestamp is an error.
* `normalize(text)` sorts the chapters by time (equal times keep their order) and writes them as `fmt_ts(ms) + " " + title` joined by `\n` (no final newline). It is an error when there are no chapters, when two chapters have the same time, or when the earliest does not start at 0.
* `durations(text, total_ms)` is the length of every chapter in sorted order: the next start minus its own start, the last one up to `total_ms`; `total_ms` must be greater than the last start (else an error).
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` is the title of the chapter that contains the time `ms` (a chapter lasts from its start up to, not including, the next start), with `0 <= ms < total_ms` (else an error); the same list rules apply.

## Functions

* `parse_ts(text)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `fmt_ts(ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`ms`: int)
* `normalize(text)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str)
* `durations(text, total_ms)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `total_ms`: int)
* `chapter_at(text, ms, total_ms)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `ms`: int, `total_ms`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Python (source)

```python
def parse_ts(text: str) -> int
def fmt_ts(ms: int) -> str
def normalize(text: str) -> str
def durations(text: str, total_ms: int) -> list[int]
def chapter_at(text: str, ms: int, total_ms: int) -> str
```

## TypeScript (target)

The TypeScript API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Module `src/chapter_marks.ts` with one `export function` per function. The test run includes `tsc -p .` with `strict` enabled, so the code must type-check. Numbers are `number`; `u32` values are non-negative integers below 2^32. Failure is signalled by throwing an exception. An absent `opt` value is `null`.

```ts
export function parseTs(text: string): number
export function fmtTs(ms: number): string
export function normalize(text: string): string
export function durations(text: string, totalMs: number): number[]
export function chapterAt(text: string, ms: number, totalMs: number): string
```

## Checking

`test/vectors.test.ts` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the TypeScript API; run `tsc -p . && node --test build/test/*.test.js`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.
